description: Define a test class containing a private static final field `EOL` of type `String` (exact initialization not required for this test), then write a parameterized test method annotated with `@ParameterizedTest` and `@ValueSource(ints = { -100, -1, 0 })` that accepts a single `int` parameter named `width`. Within the method body, instantiate a new `HelpFormatter` object by invoking its no-argument constructor, immediately chain a call to the `findWrapPos` method on this instance passing three arguments in order: the String literal `"Hello World"`, the parameter `width`, and the int literal `0`, and assign the returned `int` value to a local variable named `pos`. Following this assignment, invoke `assertEquals` passing two arguments: first the parameter `width`, then the variable `pos`, to verify that the returned position matches the input width parameter. The test uses method-level annotations `@ParameterizedTest` and `@ValueSource(ints = { -100, -1, 0 })`, employs JUnit 5 Assertions via `assertEquals`, and exercises the deprecated application class `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter` with its `findWrapPos(String, int, int)` method.

Define a test method that declares a local variable `channel` of type `WritableByteChannel` and initialize it by invoking `mock(WritableByteChannel.class)` from Mockito, then configure the mock by calling `when(channel.isOpen()).thenReturn(true)` to stub the `isOpen` method to return `true`. Next, declare a local variable `shield` of type `WritableByteChannel` and assign it the result of invoking the static method `CloseShieldChannel.wrap(channel)`, passing the mocked `channel` as the argument. Before closing the shield, stub the `write` method by calling `when(channel.write(null)).thenReturn(42)` to configure the mock to return integer `42` when `write` is invoked with `null`, then immediately invoke `shield.write(null)` and assert using `assertEquals(42, shield.write(null))` that the return value equals `42`, followed by verifying the interaction with `verify(channel).write(null)` to confirm that `write` was called on the underlying `channel` with `null` as the argument. After this verification, invoke `shield.close()` to close the shielded channel, then assert that invoking `shield.write(null)` throws a `ClosedChannelException` by using `assertThrows(ClosedChannelException.class, () -> shield.write(null))`, and finally verify that no further interactions occurred on the `channel` mock by calling `verifyNoMoreInteractions(channel)`. Annotate the test method with `@Test`, declare it to throw `Exception`, use Mockito for mocking and verification, and JUnit 5 Assertions for `assertEquals` and `assertThrows`.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that validates the behavior of the `isArch` static method from class `org.apache.commons.exec.OS` when provided with invalid architecture arguments. Begin by invoking `OS.isArch` with a `null` argument and immediately assert that the returned boolean value is `false` using `assertFalse`. Following this, invoke `OS.isArch` again, this time passing the String literal `"...."` as the argument, and assert that the returned boolean value is `false` using `assertFalse`. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with method-level annotation `@Test` and no class-level annotations.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that begins by declaring a final `Integer` variable named `integerOne` and assigning it the literal value `1662`, then declare a final `Integer` variable named `integerTwo` and assign it the literal value `1164`. Next, instantiate a `LevenshteinResults` object by invoking its constructor with four arguments—all four arguments being the variable `integerOne`—and assign the resulting instance to a final variable named `levenshteinResults`. Following this, instantiate a second `LevenshteinResults` object by invoking its constructor with four arguments in the order `integerOne`, `integerOne`, `integerTwo`, `integerTwo`, and assign this instance to a final variable named `levenshteinResultsTwo`. Then invoke the `equals` method on `levenshteinResults`, passing `levenshteinResultsTwo` as the argument, and wrap this invocation in an `assertFalse` call to verify that the equality check returns `false`. The test uses the JUnit 5 Assertions library with method-level annotation `@Test` and no class-level annotations.

Define a test method that declares a `throws` clause for `IOException` and `ImagingException`, then assign the String literal `"/images/png/IMAGING-340/image-with-exif.png"` to variable `input`, invoke `getResource(input)` on the class literal `PngReadTest.class` to obtain a `URL`, immediately chain `getFile()` on that result and assign the returned String to variable `file`, instantiate a `PngImageParser` using its no-argument constructor and assign it to variable `parser`, construct a `File` instance by passing `file` as the argument, invoke `getMetadata` on `parser` with that `File` instance, cast the returned value to `PngImageMetadata` and assign it to variable `pngMetadata`, invoke `getExif()` on `pngMetadata` and assign the resulting `TiffImageMetadata` to variable `exifMetadata`, then invoke `findDirectory` on `exifMetadata` passing the constant `TiffDirectoryConstants.DIRECTORY_TYPE_ROOT` as the argument to obtain a `TiffDirectory`, immediately chain `getFieldValue` on that directory passing the constant `TiffTagConstants.TIFF_TAG_IMAGE_DESCRIPTION` as the argument, and assert using `assertEquals` that the returned value equals the String literal `"Glavo"`, construct another `File` instance by passing `file` again, invoke `getMetadata` on `parser` with this second `File` instance, cast the result to `PngImageMetadata` and assign it to variable `metadata`, invoke `getTextualInformation()` on `metadata` to obtain an `ImageMetadata` instance, chain `getItems()` on that result to retrieve a `List`, invoke `isEmpty()` on the list and assert using `assertTrue` that it returns `true`, then invoke `getExif()` on `metadata` to obtain a `TiffImageMetadata`, chain `findDirectory` on that result passing `TiffDirectoryConstants.DIRECTORY_TYPE_ROOT`, chain `getFieldValue` on the returned `TiffDirectory` passing `TiffTagConstants.TIFF_TAG_IMAGE_DESCRIPTION`, and assert using `assertEquals` that this final value equals the String literal `"Glavo"`. The test uses the `@Test` annotation and no class-level or method-level integration annotations, relies on JUnit 5 Assertions for `assertEquals` and `assertTrue`, and does not employ any mocking libraries.

Define a test class containing two private static final fields: `TEST_STRING` of type `String` and `TEST_CHARS` of type `char[]`, initializing them with appropriate test data values. Write a test method annotated with `@Test` that begins by opening a try-with-resources block, declaring a variable `writer` of type `NullWriter` and assigning it the value `NullWriter.INSTANCE`. Within the try block, invoke `write` on `writer` passing three arguments: the char array `TEST_CHARS`, the int offset `1`, and the int length `2`. Following this invocation, use `assertThrows` to verify that an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is thrown when invoking `write` on `writer` with arguments `TEST_CHARS`, `-1`, and `0`. Next, use `assertThrows` to verify that an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is thrown when invoking `write` on `writer` with arguments `TEST_CHARS`, `0`, and `-1`. Then use `assertThrows` to verify that an `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is thrown when invoking `write` on `writer` with arguments `TEST_CHARS`, `0`, and `4`. Finally, use `assertThrows` to verify that a `NullPointerException` is thrown when invoking `write` on `writer` with a null char array explicitly cast as `(char[]) null`, offset `0`, and length `0`. The try-with-resources block automatically closes the `writer` upon completion. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with method-level annotation `@Test` and no class-level annotations.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that verifies `URIUtils.encodePath` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for invalid inputs by first invoking `assertThrows` with `IllegalArgumentException.class` as the expected exception type and a lambda expression that calls `URIUtils.encodePath` passing `null` as the first argument and the result of `StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name()` as the second argument, then immediately follow with a second `assertThrows` invocation using `IllegalArgumentException.class` as the expected exception and a lambda that calls `URIUtils.encodePath` with an empty string literal `""` as the first argument and another empty string literal `""` as the second argument. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with method-level annotation `@Test`.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that declares it throws `IOException`, beginning by initializing an `int` variable `threshold` with value `1`, then instantiating an `AtomicInteger` assigned to variable `counter` using the no-argument constructor, followed by opening a try-with-resources block that declares `ByteArrayOutputStream` variable `os` initialized via the no-argument constructor and `ThresholdingOutputStream` variable `out` initialized by invoking the three-argument constructor passing `threshold` as the first argument, a lambda expression `tos -> { counter.incrementAndGet(); tos.resetByteCount(); }` as the second argument (where the lambda body first calls `incrementAndGet()` on `counter` and then invokes `resetByteCount()` on the lambda parameter `tos`), and a lambda expression `o -> os` as the third argument. Within the try block, first invoke `assertFalse` on the result of calling `isThresholdExceeded()` on `out`, then invoke `assertEquals` with expected value equal to the result of calling `getThreshold()` on `out` and actual value `threshold`, and finally invoke `assertEquals` with expected value equal to the result of calling `getByteCount()` on `out` and actual value `0`. Next, invoke `assertEquals` with expected value `0` and actual value obtained by calling `get()` on `counter`. Invoke `write` on `out` passing the character literal `'a'` (as an int), then invoke `assertFalse` on the result of calling `isThresholdExceeded()` on `out`. Invoke `write` on `out` again with character literal `'a'`, then invoke `assertEquals` with expected value `1` and actual value from calling `get()` on `counter`, followed by invoking `assertFalse` on the result of calling `isThresholdExceeded()` on `out`. Invoke `write` on `out` with character literal `'a'`, then immediately invoke `write` on `out` again with character literal `'a'`, and finally invoke `assertEquals` with expected value `3` and actual value from calling `get()` on `counter`, allowing the try-with-resources to automatically close both `out` and `os` upon completion. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions (`assertEquals`, `assertFalse`).

Define a parameterized test method annotated with `@ParameterizedTest` and `@MethodSource("fileTimeNanoUnitsToNtfsProvider")` that accepts two parameters: a `String` named `instantStr` and a `long` named `javaTime`. Begin by creating an `Instant` object named `instant` by invoking `Instant.ofEpochMilli(javaTime)`, then immediately assert equality between `javaTime` and the result of calling `toEpochMilli()` on `instant` using `assertEquals(javaTime, instant.toEpochMilli())`. Next, invoke the static method `FileTimes.toNtfsTime(javaTime)` and assign the returned `long` value to a variable named `ntfsTime`. With this NTFS time value, invoke the static method `FileTimes.ntfsTimeToInstant(ntfsTime)` and assign the resulting `Instant` to a variable named `instant2`. Following this conversion, check whether `ntfsTime` equals `Long.MIN_VALUE` or `Long.MAX_VALUE` using an if-condition; if either condition holds true, execute an empty block (representing a scenario where `toNtfsTime` returns boundary values instead of overflowing), otherwise proceed to the else block where you assert equality between `javaTime` and the result of calling `toEpochMilli()` on `instant2` using `assertEquals(javaTime, instant2.toEpochMilli())`. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions via `assertEquals`, is annotated with `@ParameterizedTest` and `@MethodSource("fileTimeNanoUnitsToNtfsProvider")`, and relies on the application class `FileTimes` with its static methods `toNtfsTime(long)` and `ntfsTimeToInstant(long)`.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that validates the behavior of the `isVersion` static method from the `org.apache.commons.exec.OS` class by invoking `assertFalse(OS.isVersion(null))` to verify that passing `null` as the version argument returns false, then immediately invoke `assertFalse(OS.isVersion("...."))` to verify that passing the String literal `"...."` as the version argument also returns false. The test uses JUnit assertions (specifically `assertFalse` from JUnit) and operates on the static method `isVersion` of the `OS` application class without requiring any field declarations, setup methods, or teardown logic. Class-level annotations: None. Method-level annotations: `@Test`. Assertion library: JUnit. Mocking libraries: None.

Define a test class containing a private static field named `distance` of type `org.apache.commons.text.similarity.HammingDistance`, and include a setup method annotated with `@BeforeEach` that instantiates this field by invoking the no-argument constructor `new HammingDistance()` and assigns the result to `distance`. Write a test method annotated with `@Test` that verifies the behavior when a null left value is passed to the `apply` method by invoking `assertThrows` with `IllegalArgumentException.class` as the first argument and a lambda expression as the second argument, where the lambda body calls `distance.apply(null, "")` passing `null` as the first argument and an empty String literal `""` as the second argument, ensuring that the invocation throws the expected exception type. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with the `@Test` annotation at the method level.

Define a test class containing two private static final fields: `TEST_STRING` of type `String` and `TEST_CHARS` of type `char[]`, both initialized with appropriate test values. Write a test method annotated with `@Test` that begins by opening a try-with-resources block, declaring a variable `writer` of type `NullWriter` and assigning it the value `NullWriter.INSTANCE`. Within the try block, invoke `append` on `writer` passing `TEST_STRING` as the argument, then immediately assert using `assertSame` that the returned value is identical to `writer`. Following this, invoke `append` on `writer` again, this time passing `null` as the argument, and assert using `assertSame` that the returned value is again identical to `writer`. The try-with-resources block automatically closes the `writer` upon completion. This test uses the JUnit 5 Assertions library with the `@Test` annotation.

Define a test class containing two private static final fields: `TEST_STRING` of type `java.lang.String` and `TEST_CHARS` of type `char[]`, initializing them with appropriate test data values. Write a test method annotated with `@Test` that begins by declaring a try-with-resources block, assigning `NullWriter.INSTANCE` to a variable named `writer` of type `org.apache.commons.io.output.NullWriter`. Within the try block, invoke `write` on `writer` passing `TEST_STRING` as the argument, then immediately use `assertThrows` with `NullPointerException.class` as the first argument and a lambda expression as the second argument that invokes `write` on `writer` with a cast null String literal `(String) null` to verify that passing null throws the expected exception. The try-with-resources construct automatically closes the writer upon block exit. The test method uses JUnit 5 Assertions via the `assertThrows` method and is annotated with `@Test` at the method level, with no class-level annotations present.

Define a test class containing a private field `converter` of type `Converter<Enum<PizzaStatus>>` where `PizzaStatus` is an enum type defined within the test class scope. Implement a setup method annotated with `@BeforeEach` that instantiates `converter` by creating a new `EnumConverter<>()` using the no-argument constructor and assigns it to the field. Write a test method annotated with `@Test` that verifies exception handling by invoking `assertThrows` with `ConversionException.class` as the first argument and a lambda expression as the second argument, where the lambda calls `converter.convert(Enum.class, "java.lang.String#MONDAY")` passing the raw `Enum.class` type as the first parameter and the String literal `"java.lang.String#MONDAY"` as the second parameter, expecting the conversion to throw a `ConversionException` due to the non-enum class reference. Implement a teardown method annotated with `@AfterEach` that assigns `null` to the `converter` field to release the resource. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with method-level annotation `@Test`, and the setup/teardown methods throw `Exception` in their signatures.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that verifies unsupported operations when a `ChannelOrigin` is constructed with a `WritableByteChannel`. Begin by creating a mock instance of `WritableByteChannel` using `mock(WritableByteChannel.class)` and assign it to a variable named `channel` of type `Channel`. Instantiate a new `ChannelOrigin` by passing `channel` to its constructor, assigning the result to a variable named `origin` of type `ChannelOrigin`. Immediately assert that invoking `getInputStream()` on `origin` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` by calling `assertThrows(UnsupportedOperationException.class, origin::getInputStream)`. Following this, assert that invoking `getReader(null)` on `origin` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` by calling `assertThrows(UnsupportedOperationException.class, () -> origin.getReader(null))`, where the lambda captures the method call with a `null` argument. Finally, assert that invoking `getChannel(ReadableByteChannel.class)` on `origin` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` by calling `assertThrows(UnsupportedOperationException.class, () -> origin.getChannel(ReadableByteChannel.class))`, where the lambda captures the method call with the class literal `ReadableByteChannel.class` as the argument. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions via `assertThrows`, Mockito for mocking via `mock`, and the method-level annotation `@Test`.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that declares it throws `ReflectiveOperationException`, then instantiate a new `Fixture` object by invoking its no-argument constructor and assign it to variable `fixture`, followed by instantiating a new `PropertyUtilsBean` object using its no-argument constructor and assigning it to variable `propertyUtilsBean`, and immediately invoke `assertThrows` with arguments `NoSuchMethodException.class` and a lambda expression that calls `getNestedProperty` on `propertyUtilsBean` passing arguments `fixture` and the String literal `"testEnum.declaringClass.classLoader"`, verifying that this invocation throws `NoSuchMethodException` due to the default security configuration that suppresses access to the `declaringClass` property. The test uses class-level annotations: none. The test uses method-level annotations: `@Test`. The test uses assertion libraries: JUnit 5 Assertions. The test uses no mocking libraries.

Define a test class containing a static final field `EQ_FRIEND` of type `char[]`, then write a test method annotated with `@Test` that begins by instantiating a `JexlFeatures` object via `new JexlFeatures()` and immediately chaining method calls `localVar(false)`, `lambda(false)`, `loops(false)`, `sideEffect(false)`, and `sideEffectGlobal(false)` in sequence, assigning the result to a final variable `f` of type `JexlFeatures`. Next, instantiate a `JexlBuilder` via `new JexlBuilder()` and chain method calls `parserFactory(SQLParser::new)`, `cache(32)`, and `features(f)` in sequence, assigning the result to a final variable `builder` of type `JexlBuilder`. Invoke `create()` on `builder` and assign the returned `JexlEngine` instance to a final variable `sqle`. Invoke `createScript` on `sqle` with String literal `"a <> 25"` and String literal `"a"` as arguments, then immediately invoke `execute` on the returned `JexlScript` with `null` and integer literal `24` as arguments, cast the result to `boolean`, and pass it to `Assertions.assertTrue`. Invoke `createScript` on `sqle` with String literal `"a <> 25"` and String literal `"a"`, then invoke `execute` on the returned script with `null` and integer literal `25`, cast the result to `boolean`, and pass it to `Assertions.assertFalse`. Invoke `createScript` on `sqle` with String literal `"a = 25"` and String literal `"a"`, then invoke `execute` on the returned script with `null` and integer literal `24`, cast the result to `boolean`, and pass it to `Assertions.assertFalse`. Invoke `createScript` on `sqle` with String literal `"a != 25"` and String literal `"a"`, then invoke `execute` on the returned script with `null` and integer literal `24`, cast the result to `boolean`, and pass it to `Assertions.assertTrue`. Invoke `createScript` on `sqle` with String literal `"a = 25"` and String literal `"a"`, then invoke `execute` on the returned script with `null` and integer literal `25`, cast the result to `boolean`, and pass it to `Assertions.assertTrue`. Finally, invoke `createScript` on `sqle` with String literal `"a != 25"` and String literal `"a"`, then invoke `execute` on the returned script with `null` and integer literal `25`, cast the result to `boolean`, and pass it to `Assertions.assertFalse`. The test uses method-level annotation `@Test`, assertion library JUnit 5 Assertions, and no mocking libraries.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that declares `throws Exception` in its signature, then begin by invoking the static method `quoteArgument` on `org.apache.commons.exec.util.StringUtils` with the String literal `"'hi'"` and assert using `assertEquals` that the returned value equals `"hi"`. Next, invoke `quoteArgument` again with the argument `"\"hi\""` (a String containing double quotes around "hi") and assert the result equals `"hi"`. Following this, call `quoteArgument` with the String literal `"echo 'hi'"` and assert the returned value equals `"\"echo 'hi'\""` (double quotes wrapping the entire phrase). Then invoke `quoteArgument` with `"echo \"hi\""` (containing escaped double quotes) and assert the result equals `"'echo \"hi\"'"` (single quotes wrapping the phrase with escaped double quotes inside). Finally, use `assertThrows` to verify that invoking `quoteArgument` with the argument `"echo \"hi 'world'\""` (a String containing both escaped double quotes and single quotes) throws an `IllegalArgumentException`, passing the lambda expression `() -> StringUtils.quoteArgument("echo \"hi 'world'\"")` as the executable and the message `"Can't handle single and double quotes in same argument"` as the third argument. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with method-level annotation `@Test`.

Define a test class containing a private static final field `WHITESPACE` of type `java.lang.String`, then write a test method annotated with `@Test` that verifies the behavior of the `isDelimiter` static method on the `WordUtils` class by invoking it with various code point and delimiter array combinations. Begin by invoking `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with the int cast of character `'.'` and `null` as the delimiter array, then immediately assert the result is false using `assertFalse`. Next, invoke `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with the int cast of character `' '` (space) and `null` as the delimiter array, then assert the result is true using `assertTrue`. Following this, invoke `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with the int cast of character `' '` (space) and a new char array containing the single element `'.'`, then assert the result is false using `assertFalse`. Proceed by invoking `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with the int cast of character `'.'` and a new char array containing the single element `'.'`, then assert the result is true using `assertTrue`. Continue by invoking `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with the int cast of character `' '` (space) and a new char array containing three elements `'.'`, `'_'`, and `'a'`, then assert the result is false using `assertFalse`. Finally, invoke `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with the int cast of character `'.'` and a new char array containing four elements `'.'`, `'_'`, `'a'`, and `'.'`, then assert the result is true using `assertTrue`. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with method-level annotation `@Test` and no class-level annotations.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that begins by creating a `char[]` variable named `punctuation` initialized by invoking `ArraySorter.sort` on a new `char` array literal containing the exact characters `'!'`, `'\"'`, `'#'`, `'$'`, `'&'`, `'\''`, `'('`, `')'`, `','`, `'.'`, `':'`, `';'`, `'?'`, `'@'`, `'['`, `'\\'`, `']'`, `'^'`, `'_'`, `'`'`, `'{'`, `'|'`, `'}'`, and `'~'` in that order. Next, construct a `RandomStringGenerator` variable named `generator` by invoking the static method `RandomStringGenerator.builder()`, then chain `setAccumulate(true)`, followed by `withinRange('a', 'z')`, then `withinRange('A', 'Z')`, then `withinRange('0', '9')`, then `selectFrom(punctuation)`, and finally `get()` to build the generator instance. Invoke `generate(10)` on the `generator` object and assign the returned `String` to a variable named `randomText`. Iterate over each character in `randomText` by calling `toCharArray()` on it and using an enhanced for-loop with loop variable `c` of type `char`, and within the loop body, assert using `assertTrue` that the expression `Character.isLetter(c) || Character.isDigit(c) || Arrays.binarySearch(punctuation, c) >= 0` evaluates to `true`, thereby verifying each character is either a letter, a digit, or present in the sorted `punctuation` array. The test uses JUnit 5 with the `@Test` annotation and JUnit 5 Assertions for the `assertTrue` method.

Define a test method annotated with `@ParameterizedTest`, `@ValueSource(classes = { IllegalStateException.class, IllegalArgumentException.class, NullPointerException.class, RuntimeException.class })`, and `@Timeout(value = 5, unit = TimeUnit.SECONDS, threadMode = ThreadMode.SAME_THREAD)` that accepts a single parameter of type `Class<Exception>` named `throwableClass` and declares `throws ConcurrentException`. Begin by declaring a local variable `message` of type `String` initialized to the literal value `"Initializing"`. Next, declare a variable `asi` of type `AtomicSafeInitializer<Object>` and initialize it by invoking the static method `builder()` on `AtomicSafeInitializer`, then chain `setInitializer` passing a lambda expression that throws an exception created by calling `getConstructor(String.class)` on `throwableClass`, then invoking `newInstance(message)` on the returned constructor to instantiate the exception with the message, and finally chain `get()` to obtain the `AtomicSafeInitializer` instance. Immediately assert by calling `assertEquals` with `message` as the first argument and as the second argument invoke `assertThrows` passing `throwableClass` and a method reference `asi::get`, then chain `getMessage()` on the thrown exception to verify the exception message matches the expected string. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions for `assertEquals` and `assertThrows`, and the method-level annotations include `@ParameterizedTest`, `@ValueSource`, and `@Timeout` with no class-level annotations present.

Define a test method annotated with `@Test` that verifies an `IllegalArgumentException` is thrown when attempting to configure a CSV format with a line feed character as the delimiter. Define a test class containing two private static final fields: `TEST_STRING` of type `java.lang.String` and `TEST_CHARS` of type `char[]`, initialized with appropriate literal values. Define a test method that instantiates an anonymous inner class implementing the `ByteSupplier` interface by overriding its `getAsByte()` method to return the byte literal `1`, then immediately invoke `getAsByte()` on this instance and pass the returned value as the second argument to `assertEquals` with the expected value of integer `1` as the first argument, verifying that the supplier produces the correct byte value. The test uses JUnit 5 Assertions with the `@Test` annotation.

Define a test method that verifies the behavior of the `isDelimiter` method from the `WordUtils` class by executing six distinct assertion sequences. Begin by invoking `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with character `'.'` and `null` as the delimiter array, then assert that the result is `false` using `assertFalse`. Next, invoke `WordUtils.isDelimiter` with character `' '` (space) and `null` as the delimiter array, then assert that the result is `true` using `assertTrue`.
